Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out to the middle now with the sun shining brightly. Brandon King and Evin Lewis are the two openers for West Indies. Taskin Ahmed to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

West Indies now have a target of 295 runs to win the first ODI of the series. Will they be able to get it or will the Bangladesh bowlers have different ideas? Let's find out in the Run Chase! Stay tuned for what promises to be an exciting chase.

Tanzid Hasan is up for a quick chat. He says that the wicket was really good. Adds that he is enjoying his batting on these pitches. Tells that they needed a partnership after the first two wickets and they were looking to play on the merit of the ball. Mentions that it was difficult to bat in the first few overs but they knew after ten overs or so, it would settle. Ends by saying that it is a good total and that if their bowlers do the job, they will defend it.

At 198/5, Mahmudullah and Jaker Ali took charge, combining experience and aggression to mount a strong finish. Jaker's aggressive footwork and Mahmudullah's steady hand produced a crucial 96-run partnership, peppered with six sixes. The final eight overs yielded 77 runs, with the West Indian bowlers struggling to contain the flow of runs. Alzarri Joseph, Jayden Seales, and Justin Greaves bore the brunt of the late onslaught as Bangladesh finished with a big total.

Bangladesh post an imposing total of 294/6 in their 50 overs, powered by an unbeaten 50 from Mahmudullah and a solid team effort. The innings began positively with Tanzid Hasan and Soumya Sarkar setting the tone at a brisk run rate of over six per over. However, Soumya fell early, edging a delivery from Alzarri Joseph in the fifth over. Litton Das followed soon after, dismissed by Romario Shepherd, leaving Bangladesh to rebuild. Tanzid Hasan displayed intent, regularly finding the boundary, and paired up with skipper Mehidy Hasan Miraz to stabilize the innings. Despite two dropped chances by Keacy Carty, Mehidy capitalized, while Tanzid reached his fifty before falling to Alzarri Joseph, cutting to backward point. The momentum continued with Afif Hossain joining Mehidy, adding quick runs. Mehidy brought up his fifth ODI fifty off 71 balls and forged a 50-run stand with Afif. However, Afif was caught off Shepherd in the 34th over, and Mehidy soon departed for a well-made 74, mistiming a big shot off Jayden Seales.

Bangladesh finishes the First Inning at 294/6, setting up a good total for the First ODI here at St. Kitts. Brilliant batting performance by the Bangladesh batters, getting exposed to the conditions early and setting the pace of the innings throughout the 50 overs.

West Indies keep Bangladesh under 300 here! A dot to end the innings! Romario Shepherd bowls the off-cutter, on a length and around off. Rishad Hossain goes through his heave way early and misses. Bangladesh finish on 294/6!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! It is an early morning start and the crowd is still coming in at Warner Park. Shai Hope was feeling a bit unwell, but the good news for West Indies is that he is taking the field from the start. The Windies players are in a huddle, and then they spread out to take their respective field positions. Tanzid Hasan and Soumya Sarkar are the two openers for Bangladesh. Alzarri Joseph has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will start with the national anthem of St. Kitts and Nevis followed by Bangladesh's and conclude with the Rally 'Round the West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree and Curtly Ambrose analyze the pitch, noting the small boundary dimensions - 69 meters straight down the ground and 67 to 70 meters square of the wicket. They describe the surface as having a good covering of grass with a few barren patches. The pitch is hard and expected to offer some bounce, setting the stage for a balanced contest between bat and ball.

Shai Hope, the captain of West Indies says that they would have bowled first anyway. Adds that as it is an early morning start, there will be moisture and it will be a big factor but they need to exploit it well. Mentions that the England series was good but they will take one game at a time and wants to continue the momentum in this format. Says that a couple of new faces in the squad with Justin Greaves back in the ODI side and they are going with four seamers.

Mehidy Hasan, the skipper of Bangladesh says he is confident in the pitch’s potential for a high-scoring game. He emphasizes the importance of posting over 280 runs by batting longer. Reflecting on recent form, he notes their strong performances in the last few series and highlights the need to play positively against a competitive opponent. Acknowledging the absence of key senior players, Mehidy sees this as an opportunity for the younger players to step up and prove themselves. He confirms their bowling attack will feature three pacers and two spinners, aiming for a balanced approach in the series opener.
West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Evin Lewis, Keacy Carty, Shai Hope (C/WK), Sherfane Rutherford, Romario Shepherd, Justin Greaves, Gudakesh Motie, Jayden Seales, Roston Chase, Alzarri Joseph.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Soumya Sarkar, Litton Das (WK), Afif Hossain, Mahmudullah, Mehidy Hasan (C), Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Jaker Ali, Taskin Ahmed, Nahid Rana.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Mehidy Hasan. Bangladesh have elected to BAT first.

As Bangladesh aims to bounce back from their recent loss, the West Indies will look to build on their winning streak. With new players stepping up for both teams, this promises to be an exciting contest. The fact that there is nothing to choose between the teams with both winning 21 ODIs each makes this series even more interesting and unmissable. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

On the other side, Bangladesh will be led by Mehidy Hasan as regular skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto sits out due to a Grade II groin strain sustained during their previous series against Afghanistan. Towhid Hridoy is also unavailable for the series due to a similar injury. The loss of Shanto was felt during the third ODI against Afghanistan, where Bangladesh succumbed to a five-wicket defeat. Afghanistan’s Azmatullah Omarzai played a pivotal role in the result with an all-round performance, taking four wickets and scoring 70 runs to guide his team to a series-clinching victory.

West Indies enter the series with momentum, having clinched a 2-1 victory against England in their last ODI outing. A commanding eight-wicket win in the decisive match highlighted their form, with Brandon King scoring an unbeaten 102 to earn Player of the Match honors. Matthew Forde’s consistent bowling displays secured him the Player of the Series title, though his absence in this series will leave big shoes to fill.

West Indies and Bangladesh are set to transition into ODI cricket as they face off in a three-match series. A warm welcome to everyone who is joining us for the first ODI live from Warner Park in St. Kitts. The West Indies squad have suffered a setback with injuries ruling out Shamar Joseph and Matthew Forde. In their place, the young talents Marquino Mindley and Jediah Blades have been called up, both of whom delivered impressive performances in the recent Super50 domestic tournament.
